newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria adopts finance law, Zeroual seeks austerity.
newsitem.headline: Algeria adopts finance law, Zeroual seeks austerity.

text.p: Algeria's cabinet on Sunday adopted finance and budget law for 1997 which, President Liamine Zeroual said, would for the first time see a start to repayment of the public debt, the official Algerian news agency APS reported.
It gave no figures but quoted Zeroual as saying the internal public debt repayments were the fruit of austerity which must continue.
Zeroual also highlighted an increase on social spending for the poorest members of Algeria's 29 million population, saying this underlined the concern of the state for this sector.
Algeria has been engaged in a five-year-old conflict with Moslem fundamentalists whose ranks, according to officials, had been reinforced by Algerians affected by poverty.
Zeroual also called for an improvement in revenue collection and use of credits to meet the needs of the people.

Economic constraints and social difficulties must not thwart "all the efforts undertaken to renew durable economic growth, a growth which needs more sacrifice and efforts...," APS quoted the president as saying.
OPEC member Algeria has seen its reserves rise to more than $3.5 billion this year, according to Central Bank governor Abdelwahab Keramane last month.

The government said earlier this year that Algerian oil prices had risen to an average of $20.20 per barrel in the first five months of the year against $17.90 per barrel in the same period last year.
Officials have said that each extra $1 increase per barrel in crude prices gives Algeria a total of $500 million more hard currency a year.
